At Elkhorn Slough, water samples were collected using 4 collection buckets at the surface with a large-volume bucket. At each of the other stations, water samples were collected using a CTD cast, an rosette of collection bottles lowered into the water to collect samples and environmental data (temperature, salinity, oxygen, etc.) at defined depths: 0 meters, the deep chlorophyll maximum (DCM), 150 meters, and 300 meters. The DCM is the subsurface layer with the highest amount of chlorophyll, varying depending on nutrient and light availability. To allow for replication, all collections  were filtered as one liter samples three times.
